newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan navy repulses Tamil Tiger rebel attack.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan navy repulses Tamil Tiger rebel attack.

text.p: Tamil Tiger rebels attacked Sri Lankan naval boats off the country's northeastern coast early on Monday but were repulsed after a four-hour battle, a naval spokesman said.
He said an estimated 100 Sea Tigers from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) were killed and at least 10 rebel boats were sunk in the attack when the navy returned fire.

"Some 25-30 rebels boats took us about 10 miles off Mullaitivu after midnight on Sunday. They were met by an equal and strong force from our side and their flotilla was destroyed," the spokesman told Reuters.
The spokesman said one naval man died and five were wounded in the attack which began at about 1:45 a.m. (1945 GMT Sunday). Mullaitivu lies 280 km (175 miles) from the capital Colombo.
"We have sustained minor damages to our boats," the spokesman said. He did not say how many naval vessels were involved in the attack.
"Their (the rebels') remaining boats were seen limping back to Mullaitivu," the spokesman said.
An LTTE spokesman was not immediately available for comment.

The Tamil Tigers are fighting for a separate home in the island's north and east in a war now in its 14th year that the government says has claimed some 50,000 lives. The LTTE says the toll is higher.
Government troops had attacked rebel bases in the Mullaitivu jungles earlier this month. Bases of the rebels' Sea Tiger naval wing were also attacked.
Military officials then said the strikes were aimed at disrupting guerrilla preparations for an attack.
The rebels overran a key military base in the area last year, killing or capturing 1,000 soldiers in the army's worst setback in the war.
